newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian government cuts deficit in mild budget.
newsitem.headline: Australian government cuts deficit in mild budget.

text.p: The Australian government unveiled a cautious 1997/98 budget on Tuesday, making mild cuts to attack the budget deficit and boost the economy and offering modest pay-offs to average wage earners.

Treasurer Peter Costello projected an underlying deficit of A$3.85 billion (US$3.0 billion) for the year from July, down from A$6.86 billion in 1996/97 but well above market expectations of just over A$2 billion.

The underlying budget excludes windfalls such as asset sales. When assets sales and other one-off items are included, the budget delivers a A$6billion in 1998/99, said the government had turned Australia's economic fortunes around.

"The story on the economy is a good one -- we're forecasting a pick-up in growth, a pick up in employment ... and very favourable prospects not just I think for this year, but for the years ahead," he told reporters.
"Australia is now paying its way again. This is a very good effort by world standards," he said.
Voters will get A$350 million in tax rebates on income earned on savings, due to kick in next fiscal year ahead of 1999 elections. But they will have to pay more for medicines and childcare.
